title: Fujita’s conjecture
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, and let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over $k$ of dimension $n$. If $L$ is an ample line bundle on $X$, then $\box{\omega}_X \otimes L^{\otimes \ell}$ is globally generated for every integer $\ell \ge n+1$, and is very ample for every integer $\ell \ge n+2$.
completeness_reason: Canonical bundle macro corrupted; characteristic scope needs primary reconciliation.
quantifiers: All algebraically closed k, smooth projective n-fold X, ample L, all ell>=n+1 and ell>=n+2.
technical_assessment: Characteristic-zero vanishing alone cannot establish the arbitrary-characteristic global generation and very ampleness target.
source_reference: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2019/53](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/17296), page 17. Canonicalized from 5 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

completeness_reason: Semi-effective order and exact SHGH hypothesis undefined.
quantifiers: Exists one surface X and primitive F_n with unbounded orders k_n and irreducible numerical multiples k_n F_n, even under SHGH.
technical_assessment: Varying the surface is insufficient; no fixed-surface construction controls both primitive order and irreducibility.

title: Rationality and computability of Waldschmidt constants of singular points of plane curves
statement: Let $C\subset \mathbb{P}^2$ be a reduced curve, let $Z=Z_C=\operatorname{Sing}(C)$, and let $\widehat{\alpha}(Z)$ denote the Waldschmidt constant of $Z$. Must $\widehat{\alpha}(Z)$ be rational? Can it be computed? As a sample open case, take $C$ to be Klein’s arrangement of $21$ lines.

quantifiers: Every reduced plane C has rational and computable Waldschmidt constant of Sing(C).
technical_assessment: A Klein-arrangement calculation would only be an instance; uniform symbolic initial-degree control lacks a termination bound.

title: Bounded negativity for irreducible plane curves
statement:
Let $C\subset \mathbb{P}^2$ be a reduced singular plane curve, let $Z_C=\operatorname{Sing}(C)$, and let $D_C$ be the proper transform of $C$ on the blow-up of $\mathbb{P}^2$ at $Z_C$. Writing
\[
H(C)=\frac{D_C^2}{|Z_C|},
\]
if $C$ is irreducible, must one have $H(C)>-2$ in arbitrary characteristic?
completeness_reason: Curve, singular set, blowup, normalization and arbitrary characteristic are stated.
quantifiers: All irreducible reduced singular plane C in every characteristic satisfy D_C^2 divided by number of singular points >-2.
technical_assessment: Genus bounds do not supply a universal strict multiplicity bound in arbitrary characteristic; no full-scope construction or obstruction proved.

title: Brill–Noether theorem for sheaves on del Pezzo surfaces
statement:
Let $X$ be a del Pezzo surface of degree at least $4$, and let $H$ be the pullback of a line under the blowdown map $X	o\mathbb{P}^2$. Suppose $V$ is a general $(-K_X)$-semistable sheaf with numerical invariants $(r,c_1,\chi)$, and set $
u=c_1/r$. If $r\ge 2$, $\chi\ge 0$, and $
u\cdot H\ge -2$, then $V$ is nonspecial if and only if $
u\cdot C\ge -1$ for every $(-1)$-curve $C$ on $X$.
completeness_reason: Base field, moduli generality and blowdown conventions absent.
quantifiers: All degree>=4 del Pezzo X with stated blowdown, general semistable V of rank>=2, chi>=0, nu.H>=-2; nonspecial iff nu.C>=-1 for all exceptional C.
technical_assessment: Line-bundle tests do not control cohomology of general higher-rank sheaves; degree-eight model and field scope need source reconciliation.

title: Uniform doubling for all compact connected Lie groups
statement:
Conjecture: Every compact connected Lie group $K$ is uniformly doubling; that is, there exists a constant $D(K)$ such that, for every left-invariant Riemannian metric $g$ on $K$, 
\[
D_{K,g}:=\sup_{x\in K,\,r>0}\frac{\operatorname{Vol}_g(B_g(x,2r))}{\operatorname{Vol}_g(B_g(x,r))}\le D(K).
\]
completeness_reason: Metric, group dependence, all radii and uniform bound explicit.
quantifiers: Every compact connected Lie K admits D(K) controlling doubling for every left-invariant metric and all r>0.
technical_assessment: One-metric compactness gives no uniformity through collapsing metrics; finite metric sampling cannot settle it.
source_reference: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2019/54](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/17297), page 38. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Quantum optimal transport for qubits of arbitrary size
statement: For all $j\in\mathbb N$, an $j$-qubit is a state on the finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra $A_j:=\bigotimes_{n=1}^{j}M_2(\mathbb C)$. The arbitrary-size setting is the CAR algebra $A:=\bigotimes_{n=1}^{\infty}M_2(\mathbb C)$ with state space $S(A)$, consisting of all positive functionals on $A$ of norm one. How do we transport qubits of arbitrary size “optimally”?
completeness_reason: No cost, coupling class or precise optimality assertion.
quantifiers: Defines finite and infinite qubit algebras then asks how to transport optimally.
technical_assessment: Cannot replace unspecified infinite transport problem by finite-dimensional optimization.

\]
there exists some \(f\in I(0)\otimes I(0)\) such that \(h(\sigma)=h_f(\sigma)\). The corresponding transformed weight \(\widetilde h\) is also described explicitly.

quantifiers: Every displayed pre-Kuznetsov weight equals h_f for some f in I(0) tensor I(0).

statement: Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g\ge 2$. For every integer $n$ with $1\le n\le g-1$, the bounded derived category $D^b(\operatorname{Sym}^n C)$ is indecomposable; equivalently, it admits no non-trivial semiorthogonal decomposition.

statement: For every language $L$, every $L$-theory $T$, and every $L$-formula $\\varphi(x,y)$, the following are equivalent: (1) $\\varphi$ is NIP in $T$; (2) $\\varphi$ has uniform definability of types over finite sets (UDTFS) in $T$.

title: Uniform bound for the number of rational points on a curve
statement: There exists a constant $c([F:\mathbb{Q}],g)\ge 1$, depending only on the degree $[F:\mathbb{Q}]$ and $g\ge 2$, such that, for every number field $F$ and every smooth, geometrically irreducible projective curve $C$ of genus $g$ defined over $F$, $$\#C(F)\le c([F:\mathbb{Q}],g)^{1+\operatorname{rk}(\operatorname{Jac}(C)(F))}.$$

quantifiers: For every degree d>=1 and genus g>=2 exists c(d,g)>=1 bounding all C(F) by c^(1+rank Jac(C)(F)) for degree d fields.

title: Sharpness of a low-moment bound for a short zeta-function integral
statement:
Conjecture: The upper bound in Theorem 1 is sharp. Namely, for all sufficiently large $T$ and $0\le q\le 1$, the quantity
\[
\frac{1}{T}\int_T^{2T}\left(\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}\left|\zeta\left(\tfrac12+it+ih\right)\right|^2\,dh\right)^qdt
\]
should have the same order of magnitude as
\[
\left(\frac{\log T}{1+(1-q)\sqrt{\log\log T}}\right)^q.
\]
completeness_reason: Comparability constants may depend on q; required uniformity approaching one unspecified.
quantifiers: For sufficiently large T and all q in [0,1], short zeta-integral q-moment comparable to displayed logarithmic function.
technical_assessment: q=0 tautology and q=1 second moment do not imply uniform near-critical lower bounds; no full-range mechanism.

title: Fourier uniqueness from integer-radius spherical shells (nonradial case)

\]
for all \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^D\) with \(|x|^2,|y|^2\in\mathbb{Z}\), does it follow that \(\Phi=0\) everywhere?
